sec: Definition, hallmark, risk factors, sided distribution of infective endocarditis

items.exp: 'Infective endocarditis — Infection of valvular / endocardial surface'. (Book p1047)

items.q: Fill up: it involves a native / prosthetic valve or intracardiac device and 'Leads to ______ (Hallmark).'
items.exp: 'Involving Native / Prosthetic valve, Intracardiac devices → Leads to Vegetations (Hallmark).' (Book p1047)

items.q: What is printed as the hallmark of infective endocarditis?
items.exp: The definition box ends with 'Leads to Vegetations (Hallmark)'. (Book p1047)

items.q: Risk-factor groups — match — 1) Congenital 2) Rheumatic 3) Degenerative … A) Calcific degenerative aortic stenosis B) Mitral regurgitation, aortic regurgitation C) Ventricular septal defect, atrial septal defect
items.exp: 'Congenital conditions : Ventricular septal defect, Atrial septal defect'; 'Rheumatic conditions : mitral regurgitation, Aortic regurgitation'; 'Degenerative condition : Calcific degenerative aortic stenosis'. (Book p1047)

items.q: Judge the rheumatic risk note: I Mitral regurgitation and aortic regurgitation carry risk. II Mitral stenosis carries no risk.
items.exp: 'Rheumatic conditions : mitral regurgitation, Aortic regurgitation' and '· No risk with mitral stenosis'. (Book p1047)

items.q: Which rheumatic lesion is specifically printed as carrying no risk of infective endocarditis?
items.exp: '· No risk with mitral stenosis'. (Book p1047)

items.q: Which is NOT printed as a risk-factor group on this page?
items.exp: Printed groups: congenital conditions, rheumatic conditions, degenerative condition (calcific AS) and IV drug abusers. (Book p1047)

items.q: Sided distribution — match — 1) Left sided 2) Combined 3) Right sided … A) 15% B) 10%, 70% of them due to MRSA C) Most common, aortic valve, with MVP plus MR
items.exp: 'Left sided : AV (m/c), MVP + MR'; 'Combined : 15%'; 'Right sided : 10% (70% due to MRSA), Tricuspid involvement'. (Book p1047)

items.q: What share of right-sided infective endocarditis is attributed to MRSA on this page?
Right-sided disease — match — 1) Valve involved 2) Seen in … A) IV drug abusers, IV central lines B) Tricuspid
items.exp: 'Right sided … Tricuspid involvement. Seen in : IV drugs abusers, IV central lines'. (Book p1047)

items.q: Which valve is printed as the most common left-sided valve in infective endocarditis?
